Regulation: B.C. Reg. 105/2026
Made under: Carbon Tax Act
Published in: No. 12 – B.C. Regs. 99 to 109, June 30, 2026
Deposit date: June 26, 2026

B.C. Reg. 105/2026, deposited June 26, 2026, under theCARBON TAX ACT[section 84.1],COURT RULES ACT[section 1],EMPLOYER HEALTH TAX ACT[section 106.1],INSURANCE PREMIUM TAX ACT[section 42],LOGGING TAX ACT[section 43],MINERAL TAX ACT[section 44.1],MOTOR FUEL TAX ACT[section 74],PROPERTY TRANSFER TAX ACT[section 37.2],PROVINCIAL SALES TAX ACT[section 245.1],RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY(SHORT-TERM HOLDING)PROFIT TAX ACT[sections 105 and 110],SPECULATION AND VACANCY TAX ACT[section 138.1] andTOBACCO TAX ACT[section 44.11]. Order in Council 264/2026, approved and ordered June 26, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, effective October 1, 2026, (a)	the Supreme Court Civil Rules, B.C. Reg. 168/2009, are amended as set out in the attached Schedule 1, (b)	the Supreme Court Family Rules, B.C. Reg. 169/2009, are amended as set out in the attached Schedule 2, and (c)	the Tax Appeals Regulation, B.C. Reg. 135/2024, is amended as set out in the attached Schedule 3. — N. SHARMA,Attorney General and Deputy Premier; J. OSBORNE,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. 1	Rule 8-1 of the Supreme Court Civil Rules, B.C. Reg. 168/2009, is amended (a)	in subRule (1) by striking out "files" and substituting "serves", (b)	by repealing subRule (3) and substituting the following: (3)	A party wishing to apply under this rule must serve the following on each of the parties of record and on every other person, other than a party, who may be affected by the orders sought: (a)	a copy of an unfiled notice of application; (b)	a copy of any affidavit or other evidence that (i)	is to be referred to by the applicant at the hearing, and (ii)	has not already been served on that person; (c)	in the case of an application that is brought under Rule 9-7, any notice that the applicant is required to give under Rule 9-7 (9)., (c)	in subRule (4) (d) by striking out "other documents" and substituting "other evidence", (d)	by repealing subRule (4) (f) and substituting the following: (f)	subject to subrules (14.2) and (14.3), if the applicant wishes to propose a date and time for the hearing of the application, set out the proposed date and time,, (e)	by repealing subrules (5), (6), (7) and (8), (f)	by repealing subRule (9) and substituting the following:

minutes_briefs.title: BC court and tax appeal rules updated: applications now served before filing
minutes_briefs.summary: British Columbia has amended its Supreme Court Civil Rules, Supreme Court Family Rules, and the Tax Appeals Regulation. The key change is that parties applying to court must now 'serve' (deliver) their application documents to the other side before filing them with the court. This reverses the previous order of steps. The changes take effect on October 1, 2026.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you are involved in a BC Supreme Court or tax appeal case, review your procedures to ensure application documents are served on all parties before filing with the court.

key_dates.label: BC Supreme Court and tax appeal rule changes take effect

minutes_briefs.industries: Professional Services, Finance & Insurance, Natural Resources
